book.title: Dracula
book.author: Bram Stoker
book.notes: Partial key: run chapters 1-10 only (book chapters I-X). Spine order: wrap0000 (cover), h-0 (Gutenberg header), h-1 (dedication 'To my dear friend Hommy-Beg' plus contents), h-2 (the unsigned prefatory note 'How these papers have been placed in sequence...'), h-3..h-12 (run chapters 1-10). Run chapter 1 opens with the title line 'D R A C U L A' before 'CHAPTER I'. Epistolary: each journal, letter, diary or cutting has its own narrator, and a fact about a narrator comes from that narrator's own 'I' (Harker ch 1-4, Mina and Lucy letters ch 5 and 9, Seward's diary from ch 5, the Dailygraph correspondent and the Demeter's captain in ch 7). Entity types follow Annalist's vocabulary (character, place, organization, artifact, event, concept). Compare names with apostrophes folded: the text uses U+2019.

chapters.title: D R A C U L A
CHAPTER VII CUTTING FROM “THE DAILYGRAPH,” 8 AUGUST

entities.name: Jonathan Harker
entities.notes: Narrator of ch 1-4 (his shorthand journal). A newly qualified solicitor, clerk to Peter Hawkins of Exeter. Escapes the castle off-page; ch 8 finds him in a Buda-Pesth hospital.

entities.name: Mina Murray
entities.notes: Named only as 'Mina' in Harker's ch 1-4 journal; surname Murray from ch 5; 'Wilhelmina' from ch 8. Becomes Mina Harker in ch 9 (see identity_reveals). 'Madam Mina' is Van Helsing's form in later chapters, outside this key; it is listed only so full-book runs still match.

entities.name: Count Dracula
entities.notes: The calèche driver of ch 1 is the Count (suspected ch 2, concluded ch 3); see ambiguities for why that is not a scored reveal. The ship's stowaway, the great dog, the bat and Renfield's 'Master' are reader inferences only in this scope.

entities.name: Arthur Holmwood
entities.notes: Lucy's 'tall, curly-haired man' and suitor 'number Three' (ch 5). In ch 1-10 'Lord Godalming' is his father; Arthur inherits the title in run ch 13, outside this key. The alias is listed so that full-book runs are not penalised; it is excluded from matching by must_not_merge.

entities.name: Dr. John Seward
entities.notes: First described unnamed in Lucy's first ch 5 letter (the 29-year-old doctor with a lunatic asylum), named later in ch 5. Narrator of his phonograph diary from ch 5.

entities.name: Renfield
entities.notes: Seward's 'zoöphagous (life-eating) maniac' (ch 6).

entities.name: Mrs. Westenra
entities.notes: Lucy calls her 'mamma' in ch 5; named Mrs. Westenra in ch 6. Accept first_chapter 5 or 6.

entities.name: Lord Godalming
entities.notes: Arthur's father, ill throughout ch 6-10. Not Arthur in this scope.

entities.name: Mr. Swales
entities.notes: The near-hundred-year-old Whitby sailor Mina calls 'my old friend'.

entities.name: The three women
entities.notes: The three women in Castle Dracula: one fair, two dark. Modelled as one group entity; a wiki with three individual pages matches only through a group name. The text never calls them vampires or brides in this scope.

entities.name: Captain of the Demeter
entities.notes: Unnamed. Writes the ship's log, dies lashed to the wheel with a crucifix, and is buried in the Whitby churchyard. The log's 'I' is his. The Dailygraph calls his corpse 'the dead steersman'; the steersman who vanished on 30 July in the log is a different man.

entities.name: First mate of the Demeter
entities.notes: Unnamed, Roumanian. Goes mad hunting 'It' in the hold and jumps overboard on 3 August. Distinct from the second mate, who vanished on 29 July.

entities.name: Samuel F. Billington
entities.notes: Whitby solicitor of 7, The Crescent. The Count writes to him in ch 3; he takes possession of the Demeter's boxes in ch 7 and ships them to Carfax in ch 8. The firm 'Samuel F. Billington & Son' may get its own page.

entities.name: Sister Agatha
entities.notes: Nun at the Hospital of St. Joseph and Ste. Mary, Buda-Pesth, who nurses Harker.

entities.name: Szgany
entities.notes: The gipsy band who camp in the castle courtyard and work for the Count.

entities.name: Carfax
entities.notes: The Count's estate at Purfleet, with an old chapel. Seward calls it 'the deserted house' in ch 8. 'Carfax Abbey' is not in the text; it is listed for matching only.

entities.name: Hillingham
entities.notes: The Westenras' house.

entities.name: Dr. Seward's asylum
entities.notes: Ch 2 mentions 'a private lunatic asylum' next to Carfax without an owner; ch 5 says Seward runs a lunatic asylum; ch 8 shows the two grounds share a wall. A page that starts at ch 2 is fine.

entities.name: Demeter
entities.notes: Russian schooner from Varna. The 'strange ship' the coastguard watches at the end of ch 6 is very likely her, but the text does not say so; a page that starts at ch 6 is fine.

entities.name: The boxes of earth
entities.notes: Fifty boxes filled with earth from the castle chapel (ch 4), the Demeter's cargo of 'great wooden boxes filled with mould' consigned to Billington (ch 7), and the fifty boxes Billington sends to the Carfax chapel (ch 8). The text matches them by count, contents, consignee and destination; one entity.

entities.name: Harker's crucifix
entities.notes: Given to Harker at Bistritz by the landlord's wife; its beads check the Count in ch 2. A second crucifix is tied to the Demeter's wheel (ch 7); a wiki may keep them apart.

identity_reveals.rule: Mina marries Jonathan in the Buda-Pesth hospital in ch 9. Before ch 9 she is Mina Murray, his fiancée; no 'Mina Harker' name and no married_to link.

must_not_merge.rule: In ch 1-10 Lord Godalming is Arthur's ailing father, a separate person. Arthur takes the title only in run ch 13. Keep two pages.

must_not_merge.rule: Lucy (Miss Westenra) and her mother (Mrs. Westenra) share the surname. Keep two pages; the mother's heart disease and Lucy's blood loss are separate illnesses.

must_not_merge.rule: The body lashed to the wheel, which the Dailygraph calls 'the dead steersman', is the captain who wrote the log. The first mate (Roumanian) jumped overboard on 3 August; the second mate vanished on 29 July; a crewman steersman vanished on 30 July. Keep the captain and the first mate on two pages and never give the mate the corpse's name.

ambiguities: The calèche driver is the Count. Ch 1 shows a driver who calls the Count 'my master'; ch 2 has Harker half-suspect it from the handshake; ch 3 states 'it must have been the Count himself who was the driver of the coach'. Not a scored reveal: a correct ch 1 driver page names the Count as his master, and the reveal check would read that as a leak. Linking driver and Count from ch 2 or 3 is right; doing it in ch 1 runs ahead of the text.

Reader inferences that ch 1-10 never state: the tall thin stowaway and 'It'/'Him' of the Demeter's log, the great dog that leaps ashore at Whitby, the bat at Lucy's window and over the asylum, the 'something long and black' with red eyes on the churchyard seat, and Renfield's 'Master' are all the Count. A wiki may hint at these, but merging them into the Count's page, or a fact such as 'the Count bit Lucy', runs ahead of the text in this scope.
The punctures on Lucy's throat: Mina blames her own safety-pin (ch 8); Seward and Van Helsing find two punctures but name no cause (ch 10). 'Bitten by a vampire' is inference.
The word 'vampire' appears once, in ch 1, as Harker's dictionary gloss of a peasant word. No one in ch 1-10 calls the Count or the three women vampires. Not scored.
The Russian ship the coastguard watches at the end of ch 6 is almost certainly the Demeter, but the text does not join them. Demeter's first_chapter is 7; a page from ch 6 passes.

Billington's 'our client' and the Carfax 'proprietor' in the ch 8 letters are the Count by inference from the ch 3 letter to Billington and the ch 2 purchase. The boxes are one artifact because ch 4, 7 and 8 match them by count, earth, consignee and the Carfax chapel.

Harker and Mina: affection shows in ch 1-4, the engagement is stated in ch 5, and they marry in ch 9. The scorer's early check treats any romance row as the same tie, so the pair has one lenient relation and the marriage is scored through the 'Mina Harker' reveal.

Lucy's suitor 'number Three' is Arthur: her P.S. does not name him, but the same ch 5 letter says she would tell Arthur as a woman tells her husband, and Quincey's ch 5 letter toasts Arthur as the man who won her. First_chapter 5.

Seward's asylum: ch 2 mentions a private lunatic asylum next to Carfax with no owner; ch 5 says Seward runs a lunatic asylum; ch 8 shows the grounds share a wall. The borders relation is first_chapter 8, but a row from ch 2 on the same page is text-supported and passes.

Count Dracula's status in ch 4: Harker finds him in a box 'either dead or asleep', then the head turns and the eyes open. He is not dead. 'alive' is the only active value in Annalist's status vocabulary.

The first mate jumps into the sea in fog and is not seen again: 'dead' and 'missing' both pass. The captain suspects the mate killed the crew, and the inquest leaves open whether the captain did; neither suspicion is fact.
Lucy at ch 10 and Mrs. Westenra at ch 8 are alive. Both die later in the book; any death status within ch 1-10 is a leak.
Arthur becomes Lord Godalming in run ch 13. The alias is listed on Arthur so full-book runs are not failed for carrying it, but in ch 1-10 the name means his father.
The fair woman in the castle whose face Harker 'seemed somehow to know' is never identified in this scope.
